title: UP BOARD CLASS 2 — Environmental Studies | Our Family Community
description: Subject-wise test on Our Family Community (Environmental Studies) for UP BOARD CLASS 2. 50Q.
subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Who helps us when we are sick and need medicine?

options.explanation: A teacher educates students in a school setting.
A doctor treats sick people and gives them medicine to get better.
A postman delivers mail and packages.
A tailor makes and repairs clothing.

questions.explanation: A doctor treats sick people and gives them medicine to get better.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Where do children usually go to learn and study every day?

options.explanation: A market is a place where people buy and sell goods.
A hospital is a place where people go for medical treatment.
Children go to school to receive education and learn new things from teachers.
A park is a place for recreation and leisure activities.

questions.explanation: Children go to school to receive education and learn new things from teachers.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What do we call the group of people living together in one house, usually related to each other?

options.explanation: Friends are people who have a close relationship but may not live together.
Neighbours are people who live nearby but not in the same house.
A family consists of members, often related by blood or marriage, who live together and care for each other.
Strangers are people who do not know each other.

questions.explanation: A family consists of members, often related by blood or marriage, who live together and care for each other.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is a good habit for children to show at home?

options.explanation: Fighting with siblings is not a good habit and can lead to conflict.
Not listening to parents is not a good habit and can lead to disobedience.
Helping parents with small chores is a good habit that shows responsibility and respect.
Making a big mess is not a good habit and can lead to disorganization.

questions.explanation: Helping parents with small chores is a good habit that shows responsibility and respect.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: If you see a lot of garbage scattered on the road in your neighbourhood, what should you do?

options.explanation: Ignoring the garbage does not help to keep the surroundings clean.
Throwing more garbage on it will make the situation worse.

options.text: Tell an elder to help put it in a dustbin
options.explanation: Informing an elder to properly dispose of the garbage is the correct and safe action.
Playing near the garbage can be harmful and unhygienic.

questions.explanation: It's important to keep our surroundings clean. For a Class 2 child, informing an elder to properly dispose of the garbage is the correct and safe action.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which community helper delivers letters and parcels to our homes?

options.explanation: A policeman's job is to maintain law and order.
A firefighter's job is to put out fires and rescue people.
A postman's job is specifically to collect and deliver mail and packages.
A sweeper's job is to clean streets and public areas.

questions.explanation: A postman's job is specifically to collect and deliver mail and packages.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Why is it important to share our toys and things with our siblings or friends?

options.explanation: Sharing is not about letting others break our things.

options.text: It makes everyone happy and we learn to share
options.explanation: Sharing is a good habit that promotes happiness, friendship, and teaches us to be generous and cooperative.

options.text: Because we don't want them anymore
options.explanation: Sharing is not just about getting rid of things we don't want.

options.text: To show off our new toys
options.explanation: Sharing is not about showing off our things.

questions.explanation: Sharing is a good habit that promotes happiness, friendship, and teaches us to be generous and cooperative.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these activities helps a family spend quality time together?

options.text: Everyone watching TV alone in different rooms
options.explanation: Watching TV alone in different rooms does not promote family interaction.
Playing games together is an interactive activity that allows family members to communicate, laugh, and bond.

options.text: Staying silent and not talking to each other
options.explanation: Staying silent and not talking to each other does not promote family interaction.

options.text: Each person doing their own work without interaction
options.explanation: Doing individual work without interaction does not promote family bonding.

questions.explanation: Playing games together is an interactive activity that allows family members to communicate, laugh, and bond, thus spending quality time.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Your neighbour, Mrs. Singh, is an elderly person living alone. One day, you notice her newspaper has been lying outside her door for a long time and she hasn't come out. What is the most helpful thing you can do?

options.explanation: Taking the newspaper for yourself is not a helpful or considerate action.

options.text: Gently ring her doorbell and offer to bring the newspaper inside
options.explanation: Offering polite and safe help to an elderly neighbour by ringing the bell and offering to bring in their newspaper demonstrates kindness and community spirit.

options.text: Ignore it and go play with your friends
options.explanation: Ignoring the situation does not show concern for the neighbour's well-being.

options.text: Shout loudly from your house to see if she answers
options.explanation: Shouting loudly may startle or disturb the neighbour and is not a polite way to offer help.

questions.explanation: Offering polite and safe help to an elderly neighbour by ringing the bell and offering to bring in their newspaper demonstrates kindness and community spirit.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Why do we need rules in places like our school, home, or park, such as 'Don't talk loudly in the library' or 'Wait for your turn on the swing'?

options.text: To make us sad and stop our fun
options.explanation: Rules are not intended to make us sad or stop our fun.

options.text: To make things difficult and confusing for everyone
options.explanation: Rules are intended to make things clearer and more organized, not difficult and confusing.

options.text: To keep everyone safe and make things fair for all
options.explanation: Rules are put in place to ensure safety, maintain order, prevent chaos, and ensure that everyone has a fair and enjoyable experience.

options.text: So that only some special people can enjoy
options.explanation: Rules are intended to be fair and apply to everyone, not just some special people.

questions.explanation: Rules are put in place to ensure safety, maintain order, prevent chaos, and ensure that everyone has a fair and enjoyable experience.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Who usually prepares food for the family members at home?

options.explanation: Fathers may help with cooking, but it's not their primary role in most families.
Brothers may help with cooking, but it's not their primary role in most families.
In many families, the mother is primarily responsible for cooking food for the family.
Sisters may help with cooking, but it's not their primary role in most families.

questions.explanation: In many families, the mother is primarily responsible for cooking food for the family.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: If you want to send a letter to your friend, who will deliver it for you?

options.explanation: Doctors are medical professionals and do not deliver mail.
A postman is a community helper whose job is to collect and deliver letters and parcels.
Teachers are educators and do not deliver mail.
Policemen are law enforcement officers and do not deliver mail.

questions.explanation: A postman is a community helper whose job is to collect and deliver letters and parcels.

questions.question: What is the best way to keep your neighbourhood clean?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road can lead to pollution and harm the environment.
Leaving waste everywhere can lead to pollution and harm the environment.
Putting garbage in a dustbin is essential to keep our surroundings clean and prevent the spread of diseases.

options.text: Burn dry leaves in the open
options.explanation: Burning dry leaves in the open can lead to air pollution and harm the environment.

questions.explanation: Putting garbage in a dustbin is essential to keep our surroundings clean and prevent the spread of diseases.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What should you say when an elder helps you with something?

options.explanation: Saying "Sorry" is used to apologize, not to show gratitude.
Saying "Please" is used to make a request, not to show gratitude.
Saying "Thank You" is a good habit that shows politeness and gratitude when someone helps you.
Saying "Excuse Me" is used to get someone's attention or to apologize, not to show gratitude.

questions.explanation: Saying "Thank You" is a good habit that shows politeness and gratitude when someone helps you.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these places in your neighbourhood is important if you fall sick?

options.explanation: Schools are places where children go to learn, not to receive medical treatment.
Markets are places where people go to buy goods, not to receive medical treatment.
A hospital is a place where sick or injured people go to receive medical treatment from doctors and nurses.
Parks are places where people go to play or relax, not to receive medical treatment.

questions.explanation: A hospital is a place where sick or injured people go to receive medical treatment from doctors and nurses.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which type of family has parents and their children living together, without grandparents, uncles, or aunts?

options.explanation: A joint family consists of multiple generations living together, including grandparents, uncles, and aunts.
A nuclear family consists of only parents and their children living together.
A big family can refer to a large family with many children, but it does not specify the type of family structure.
An extended family consists of multiple generations and relatives living together, including grandparents, uncles, and aunts.

questions.explanation: A nuclear family consists of only parents and their children living together.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What is a good habit to follow when you are eating with your family?

options.text: Talk loudly with your mouth full
options.explanation: Talking loudly with your mouth full is impolite and can be distracting to others.
Wasting food is not only impolite but also a waste of resources.

options.text: Chew your food with your mouth closed
options.explanation: Chewing food with your mouth closed is a good table manner that shows respect and is hygienic.

options.text: Use your hands to eat all food
options.explanation: Using your hands to eat all food can be impolite and unhygienic, especially in formal settings.

questions.explanation: Chewing food with your mouth closed is a good table manner that shows respect and is hygienic.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Why is it important to play together with your friends in the park?

options.explanation: Fighting over toys is not a positive or healthy way to interact with others.
Making others sad is not a positive or healthy way to interact with others.

options.text: To learn sharing and make new friends
options.explanation: Playing together helps children learn to share, cooperate, and build friendships, which are important social skills.
Always trying to win every game can lead to an unhealthy competitive spirit and neglect the value of teamwork and cooperation.

questions.explanation: Playing together helps children learn to share, cooperate, and build friendships, which are important social skills.

questions.question: Imagine your younger brother wants to play with your new toy car. What is the kindest thing to do?

options.explanation: Hiding the toy from your brother can lead to feelings of exclusion and hurt his feelings.

options.text: Tell him he cannot touch it.
options.explanation: Telling your brother he cannot touch the toy can lead to feelings of exclusion and hurt his feelings.

options.text: Share the toy with him and play together.
options.explanation: Sharing toys with siblings is a kind act that promotes love and harmony within the family.

options.text: Break the toy so he can't play.
options.explanation: Breaking the toy is a destructive and hurtful act that can damage the relationship with your brother.

questions.explanation: Sharing toys with siblings is a kind act that promotes love and harmony within the family.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: You see a new family moving into your neighbourhood. What is a good way to welcome them?

options.explanation: Ignoring new neighbours can lead to feelings of exclusion and make them feel unwelcome.

options.text: Greet them with a smile and say hello.
options.explanation: Greeting new neighbours with a smile and a friendly hello is a good habit that shows hospitality and helps build a friendly community.

options.text: Ask them to leave the neighbourhood.
options.explanation: Asking new neighbours to leave the neighbourhood is not only impolite but also unwelcoming.

options.text: Make fun of their moving boxes.
options.explanation: Making fun of new neighbours' moving boxes can lead to feelings of embarrassment and hurt their feelings.

questions.explanation: Greeting new neighbours with a smile and a friendly hello is a good habit that shows hospitality and helps build a friendly community.

questions.question: Who are the people who live together with us in our home?

options.explanation: Friends may visit, but they do not usually live with us in our home.
Teachers do not live in our homes; they teach us in school.
Family members are the people who live together in our home and are related to us.

questions.question: If you have a fever and feel unwell, where should your parents take you for treatment?

options.explanation: School is not a place for medical treatment.
A post office is for mailing letters and parcels, not for medical treatment.
A hospital is a place where sick people go to receive medical treatment from doctors and nurses.

questions.question: What is the main role of a teacher in a school?

options.explanation: Catching thieves is not the main role of a teacher.
Delivering letters is not a teacher's responsibility.

questions.question: Which of these is a good habit for keeping your surroundings clean?

options.explanation: Throwing garbage on the road makes the surroundings dirty.
Leaving toys scattered makes the home untidy.

questions.question: Who is usually responsible for preparing meals for the family?

options.explanation: A baby is too young to prepare meals.
Parents, typically the mother or father, are usually responsible for cooking and providing meals for the family.

questions.question: Why is it important to help your family members with chores like tidying up?

options.text: So you can get more toys.

options.explanation: Doing homework is not related to helping with chores.

options.explanation: A school bag is not a way to identify a police officer.
A cooking apron is not part of a police officer's uniform.
